messages:
Maria: heads up, spotted a regression on sm86 INT4 path for very long contexts (seq=12288). p50 jumped from ~130ms to ~310ms, throughput down ~35%. saw higher mem and more GC-like stalls. cc @Sam @Devon
Sam: which workload? job id + logs?
Maria: job 3589, model: redwood-13b, run details:
```
model: redwood-13b
arch: sm86
quant: int4
seq: 12288
p50: 310ms (baseline 130ms)
tokens/s: 660 (baseline 1020)
mem_delta: +1.6GB
stack: int4_block_gemm -> int4_decode -> kv_insert
```
perf-bot: nightly-bench/3589 uploaded: https://ci.redwood/bench/3589 (contains perf traces)
Devon: autotune trace shows a kernel flip during the last autotune pass: `gemm_int4_vecs_v3` chosen for large-seq with block_size=16 and workspace=72MB. Previously we favored `gemm_fp8_blk` for >8k sequences.
Indra: our KV metrics also show more partial-cache writes, hit-rate dropped ~10%. suspect decode+memcpy overhead for int4 path with large blocks; workspace zeroing + allocator lock contention might be contributing.
Sam: sounds like autotuner is overfitting to short warmups. We only ran 100 iterations before choosing kernel. For big sequences we need longer warmups and an alloc-time measurement.
Devon: agreed. propose autotuner change: measure three dimensions per candidate: steady-state latency, workspace_alloc_ms, and kv_write_penalty. Then compute score = latency + alpha*alloc_ms + beta*kv_penalty where alpha/beta are arch-specific. Example seed for sm86:
```
autotuner_defaults:
  arch: sm86
  warmup_iters: 400
  sample_iters: 800
  scoring_factors:
    latency: 1.0
    alloc_ms: 0.6
    kv_write_penalty: 1.0
  seqlen_buckets: [256, 2048, 8192]
  prefer:
    <=2048: int8_like
    2049-8192: fp8_block
    >8192: fp8_block
```
Maria: also noticed our batching heuristic lets max_batch_tokens grow unbounded for long sequences which amplifies workspace needs. quick fix: cap max_batch_tokens for seq>8192 to 49152 on sm86.
Sam: +1; that will limit worst-case allocs while we fix autotuner. Also we should record kernel-change annotations in Rollout/Console so SRE can correlate perf spikes to kernel flips.
Indra: adding kv-hit-rate, kv-write-count, and kernel-selected as console metrics makes sense. I'll add a small probe in runtime to emit those tags.
Devon: ran a small repro harness comparing configs:
```
config X: int4_v3 block=16 workspace=72MB -> p50 310ms p99 1200ms
config Y: int4_v2 block=8 workspace=28MB  -> p50 150ms p99 300ms
config Z: fp8_block -> p50 125ms p99 260ms
```
Maria: big gap. So two immediate actions: (1) tweak autotuner scoring + increase warmups for large-seq candidates; (2) revert the aggressive block=16 default for int4 on sm86 and fallback to block=8. I'll open PRs.
Maria: PRs created: #4720 (autotune: add alloc/kv scoring & seqlen buckets), #4721 (runtime: revert int4 block16 default, add max_batch_tokens cap). @Indra please review metric probe in #4721.
Indra: reviewing now. Also recommend seeding autotuner with arch priors so it doesn't flip kernels on noisy benches; sm90 should keep int8 preference for medium seqs.
perf-bot: canary launched: canary-3480 (sm86-only, seq bucket >8k), estimated run time 1h45m. monitor: https://ci.redwood/canary/3480
Sam: plan: run canary, collect p50/p95/p99, tokens/s, mem, kv-hit-rate. Rollout plan: feature-flag behind FF-INT4-LONGSEQ, canary -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% with auto-rollback on p95 > +12% vs baseline.
Devon: one more tweak: add a light penalty for workspace >32MB in scoring to prefer smaller working sets when delta is small. prevents noisy flips when latency differences are <5%.
Maria: ok I'll update #4720 with that and add unit tests for scoring arithmetic + integration test that verifies kernel-change shows up in console traces.
Sam: nice. after canary completes, send summary to #eng-runtime and tag #sre for coordinated rollout window. :thumbsup:
